title_en: Guo Yi v. Jiangsu Yifeng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. — labor dispute
ruling_gist_en: Where a college student who is about to graduate signs a labor contract with an employer for the purpose of employment, accepts the management of the employer, and performs work as agreed in the contract, and the employer, with knowledge that the job seeker is a current student, nevertheless enters into the labor contract with the student and pays him or her labor remuneration, the labor contract is legally valid, and it shall be determined that a labor relationship has been formed between the parties.

full_text_en:
Guo Yi v. Jiangsu Yifeng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. — Labor Dispute

【Ruling Summary】

Where a college student who is about to graduate enters into a labor contract with an employer for the purpose of employment, accepts the employer's management, and performs labor as agreed in the contract; and where the employer, knowing that the job seeker is a current student, nonetheless enters into the labor contract with him and pays him labor remuneration, such labor contract is lawful and valid, and it shall be determined that a labor contract relationship is formed between the two parties.

Plaintiff: Guo Yi, male, 22 years old, residing at Nanjing, Chadian Renyuan.

Defendant: Jiangsu Yifeng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hanzhong Road, Baixia District, Nanjing.

Legal Representative: Gao Yi, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Guo Yi filed an action with the Baixia District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Jiangsu Yifeng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yifeng Company) concerning a labor dispute.

Plaintiff Guo Yi alleged: The plaintiff is a 2008 graduate of Nanjing Mochou Vocational Senior High School. In October 2007, the plaintiff submitted a job application to the defendant, and after review by the defendant's Human Resources Department and General Manager, was approved for a probationary period. On October 30, 2007, the two parties signed a labor contract for a term of three years, from October 30, 2007 to December 30, 2010. In July 2008, the defendant Yifeng Company, on the ground that it disputed the existence of a labor relationship between the plaintiff and itself, filed an arbitration application with the Nanjing Baixia District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee, requesting a determination that no labor relationship existed between the parties. On August 19, 2008, the Nanjing Baixia District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee issued an arbitration decision, concluding the arbitration proceedings on the grounds that the plaintiff was a current student, did not meet the employment conditions, lacked the subject qualification to establish a labor relationship, and that the dispute between the parties was not within the scope of labor dispute resolution. The plaintiff, dissatisfied with this decision, believed that a labor relationship existed between the parties and that the labor contract signed by them was genuine, lawful, and valid, and requested the court to confirm that the labor contract between the parties was valid.

Defendant Yifeng Company argued: At the time the plaintiff Guo Yi signed the labor contract with the defendant, his status was that of a current student. According to the provisions of the former Ministry of Labor's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China", current students do not have the subject qualification for a labor relationship. The "Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance" also does not include current students within the scope of insurance coverage, which fully indicates that current students do not fall within the category of laborers. Additionally, the plaintiff did not meet the recruitment conditions stipulated in the contract. The recruitment conditions set forth in the defendant's recruitment brochure and the labor contract signed with the plaintiff required a secondary specialized school education or higher, but the plaintiff did not graduate until July 2008, and therefore did not meet the defendant's recruitment conditions at the time of signing. Therefore, the contract between the parties was in name a labor contract but in substance a practice contract, and the relationship established between the parties was not a labor relationship and was not governed by the labor legal relationship adjusted by the Labor Law. The defendant requested that the plaintiff's action be dismissed in accordance with the law.

The Baixia District People's Court of Nanjing found the following facts at first instance:

The plaintiff, Guo Yi, was a 2008 graduate majoring in pharmacy at Jiangsu Radio and Television University (Nanjing Mochou Secondary Vocational School campus), and graduated in July 2008. On October 26, 2007, the plaintiff Guo Yi registered with the defendant Yifeng Company for employment, and in the defendant's job applicant registration form, he indicated that he was a 2008 graduate of Nanjing Mochou Vocational Senior High School and that 2007 was his internship year. On October 30, 2007, the plaintiff and the defendant signed a labor contract for a term of three years, from October 30, 2007 to December 30, 2010; the probationary period was 60 days, from October 30, 2007 to December 30, 2007. The contract also stipulated that one of the recruitment conditions was having a secondary specialized school education or higher; the plaintiff was to work as a sales clerk; after the probationary period, the monthly salary would be no less than RMB 900, and the salary during the probationary period would be no less than 80% of the salary of workers in the same type of work and position, etc. On July 21, 2008, the defendant filed an arbitration application with the Nanjing Baixia District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee, requesting a determination that no labor relationship existed between it and the plaintiff. Upon review, the Nanjing Baixia District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee, based on the former Ministry of Labor's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China", issued an arbitration decision on August 19, 2008, concluding the arbitration proceedings on the grounds that the plaintiff was a current student, did not meet the employment conditions, lacked the subject qualification to establish a labor relationship, and that the relationship between current students engaged in work-study or internship and employers was not within the scope of adjustment of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, and therefore the dispute between the defendant and the plaintiff was not within the scope of labor dispute resolution. The arbitration decision was served on August 27, 2008.

It was also found that the defendant Yifeng Company was originally named Jiangsu Yifeng Pharmacy Co., Ltd., and on July 21, 2008, was renamed Jiangsu Yifeng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. after approval by the Baixia Branch of the Nanjing Administration for Industry and Commerce.

The above facts were confirmed by statements of both parties, the job applicant registration form, the labor contract, the arbitration application, the arbitration decision, the recruitment brochure, the certificate from Nanjing Mochou Secondary Vocational School, the graduation certificate from Jiangsu Radio and Television University, and the notice of approval for company name change, and were sufficient to be established.

The dispute at first instance in this case was: whether the labor contract signed between the plaintiff Guo Yi and the defendant Yifeng Company was valid.

The Baixia District People's Court of Nanjing held at first instance:

First, to determine whether the labor contract signed between the plaintiff Guo Yi and the defendant Yifeng Company was valid, it was necessary to examine whether the plaintiff Guo Yi possessed the subject qualification for a labor relationship. At the time of signing the labor contract with the defendant Yifeng Company, the plaintiff Guo Yi was over 19 years old, meeting the employment age stipulated by the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, and possessed the capacity for conduct and responsibility to establish a labor relationship with an employer. Article 4 of the former Ministry of Labor's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the Opinions) only specified that civil servants and personnel of institutions and social organizations that implement the civil servant system by analogy, as well as rural laborers, active-duty military personnel, and domestic helpers, were not subject to the Labor Law, and did not exclude current students; student status did not automatically restrict Guo Yi from joining the labor force as an ordinary laborer. Article 12 of the Opinions provides: "Where current students engage in work-study during their spare time, it is not considered employment, and no labor relationship is established, and a labor contract may not be required to be signed." This provision applies only to the conduct of work-study by current students and cannot be used to deny the labor rights of current students or to infer that current students lack the subject qualification for a labor relationship. In summary, the law does not expressly provide that current students lack the subject qualification for a labor relationship, so the plaintiff was capable of becoming a subject of a labor relationship.

Second, the conduct of the plaintiff Guo Yi working for the defendant Yifeng Company did not fall within the circumstances specified in Article 12 of the Opinions. That provision is directed at situations where students are still primarily engaged in study at school, without the purpose of employment, and use their spare time for social practice or part-time work to subsidize tuition and living expenses. In work-study and internships, students do not establish a labor relationship with the unit, and a labor contract may not be required, and there is no need to specify positions, remuneration, benefits, etc. In this case, Guo Yi's situation clearly was not work-study or an internship. When Guo Yi registered for employment, he had completed all his study tasks, clearly expressed to Yifeng Company his desire for employment, and the two parties signed a labor contract. After signing the labor contract with Yifeng Company, Guo Yi also performed labor for Yifeng Company as stipulated, and Yifeng Company paid Guo Yi labor remuneration and managed him, which fully conformed to the essential characteristics of a labor relationship. Therefore, Yifeng Company's argument that the relationship was an internship could not be sustained.

Third, although the plaintiff Guo Yi did not meet the recruitment conditions required by the defendant Yifeng Company at the time of signing, when Guo Yi filled out Yifeng Company's job applicant registration form, he clearly informed Yifeng Company that he was a 2008 graduate, that 2007 was the school-prescribed internship year, that he could work normally, but he had not yet graduated. Yifeng Company was fully aware of this situation, and on this basis, the two parties reached an agreement on application and recruitment and signed the labor contract. Therefore, the signing of the labor contract was a genuine expression of the parties' intentions, without any fraud, concealment, coercion, or other circumstances, and did not violate laws or administrative regulations. Moreover, Guo Yi had obtained his graduation certificate in July 2008, so Yifeng Company's argument that Guo Yi did not meet the recruitment conditions also could not be sustained.

In summary, a labor relationship existed between the plaintiff Guo Yi and the defendant Yifeng Company, and the labor contract signed by the two parties was lawful and valid and had legal binding force on both parties. Accordingly, the Baixia District People's Court of Nanjing, pursuant to Articles 17 and 18 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on November 18, 2008:

The labor contract signed between the plaintiff Guo Yi and the defendant Yifeng Company on October 30, 2007, is valid.

Yifeng Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, arguing: (1) The appellee Guo Yi's status was that of a current student, and during his internship period, social insurance could not be processed for him, and this relationship was also not within the scope of adjustment of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China; therefore, the appellee lacked the subject qualification for a labor relationship. (2) The first-instance judgment confirming the existence of a labor relationship between the parties was manifestly unfair. Since the appellee was a current student, the labor and social security authorities would not process social insurance, and the appellant would bear corresponding legal liability and significant risks.

The appellee Guo Yi argued: The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law and should be affirmed.

After hearing the appeal, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held on appeal:

An internship is for the purpose of learning, involving participation in social practice at a relevant unit, without salary, and there is no situation where the intern signs a labor contract with the unit specifying position, remuneration, benefits, etc. In this case, although the appellee Guo Yi graduated in July 2008, on October 26, 2007, he clearly expressed to the appellant Yifeng Company his desire for employment, registered for employment, and in the job applicant registration form indicated that he was a 2008 graduate and that 2007 was his internship year. On October 30, 2007, Guo Yi and Yifeng Company voluntarily signed a labor contract. Yifeng Company was fully aware of Guo Yi's circumstances, and on this basis the parties reached an agreement on application and recruitment, signed the labor contract, and specified the position and remuneration. This situation should not be considered an internship. At the time of signing the labor contract with Yifeng Company, Guo Yi was over 19 years old, meeting the employment age stipulated by the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, and possessed the capacity for conduct and responsibility to establish a labor relationship with an employer. Article 12 of the Opinions cannot be used to infer that current students lack the subject qualification for a labor relationship. Therefore, the appellant's above reasons could not be sustained.

Regarding the appellant Yifeng Company's ground of appeal that confirming the validity of the labor relationship between the parties was manifestly unfair, the court held that the labor contract signed between Yifeng Company and Guo Yi was a genuine expression of the parties' intentions, and there was no significant imbalance of interests between the parties, so it should not be considered manifestly unfair.

In summary, the labor contract signed between the appellant Yifeng Company and the appellee Guo Yi was a genuine expression of the parties' intentions, did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations, was lawful and valid, and had legal binding force on both parties. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and proper trial procedures, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on April 7, 2009:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
